narrative.coaching_note: The biggest change to make is to clean your hands after you leave the bedside before you touch anything outside that area. You touched bed rail A with your bare hand starting at 0.5 seconds, and that moved contamination onto your bare hand. You then touched call button starting at 3.4 seconds, which moved contamination onto call button. You then touched phone starting at 6.6 seconds, which moved contamination onto phone in the healthcare area. Later you put on gloves at 10.9 seconds and touched bed rail A with your gloved hand starting at 11.1 seconds, and you missed another after-contact moment at 18.7 seconds after touching call button. Cleaning your hands at those after-contact times stops germs from travelling from the bedside to shared items.
narrative.audit_summary: The clip shows MRSA transfer originating from bed rail A. Bare hand contacted bed rail A at 0.5 seconds, resulting in transfer to bare hand, then to call button at 3.4 seconds and to phone at 6.6 seconds. After glove donning at 10.9 seconds, gloved hand contacted bed rail A at 11.1 seconds with transfer from bed rail A to gloved hand. Two Moment 5 opportunities were missed: bare hand at 5.8 seconds and gloved hand at 18.7 seconds. No hygiene events occurred. End contamination included bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, and phone. No resident exposures were listed. Alcohol rub and soap and water are both effective against MRSA per the analysis. Heuristic exposure score was 10.
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene for Moment 5 at 5.8 seconds.
